name: Insecure use of pickle module import
explain: The pickle module can execute arbitrary code during deserialization and may introduce security risks if misused.
fix: Avoid using pickle with untrusted data. Use safer serialization formats such as JSON.

name: SQL Injection via string-based query construction
explain: User input is directly embedded into an SQL query, which can allow attackers to manipulate database queries.
fix: Use parameterized queries or Django ORM to safely handle user input.

name: Unsafe deserialization using pickle.loads
explain: pickle.loads may execute arbitrary code when deserializing untrusted data.
fix: Replace pickle with safe deserialization methods such as JSON parsing.

name: Weak cryptographic hash algorithm (MD5)
explain: MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for security-sensitive operations such as tokens.
fix: Use SHA-256 or Django’s built-in token generation utilities.
tags: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

name: SQL Injection in coupon query
explain: Direct insertion of user input into SQL queries can lead to SQL injection attacks.
fix: Use parameterized queries or ORM methods.

name: Use of subprocess module
explain: The subprocess module may allow execution of system commands if improperly used.
fix: Avoid subprocess where possible or strictly validate inputs.

name: SQL Injection using dynamic table and column names
explain: Dynamic SQL construction using user input can be exploited to manipulate database queries.
fix: Whitelist allowed values and avoid dynamic SQL where possible.

name: Insecure hardcoded temporary directory
explain: Using predictable temporary directories may allow attackers to overwrite files or perform race-condition attacks.
fix: Use Python tempfile module for secure temporary file handling.

name: Command injection via subprocess with shell=True
explain: Using shell=True allows attackers to inject arbitrary system commands.
fix: Avoid shell=True and pass command arguments as a list.

name: Use of eval on potentially unsafe input
explain: eval executes arbitrary Python code, leading to possible remote code execution.
fix: Replace eval with ast.literal_eval or strict input validation.

name: Hardcoded Django secret key
explain: Hardcoding secret keys in source code may expose sensitive credentials.
fix: Store secret keys in environment variables.

name: Unsafe XML parsing library usage
explain: xml.etree.ElementTree is vulnerable to XML-based attacks when parsing untrusted data.
fix: Use defusedxml to safely parse XML.

name: SQL Injection in order search query
explain: Embedding user input into SQL queries can result in SQL injection.
fix: Use parameterized queries or ORM filters.

name: Unsafe XML parsing using fromstring
explain: Parsing untrusted XML without protections may lead to XXE attacks.

name: Unsafe YAML deserialization
explain: yaml.load allows arbitrary object instantiation and may lead to code execution.

name: Use of subprocess module in products views
explain: The subprocess module can be dangerous if used with unsanitized input.
fix: Avoid subprocess or validate inputs strictly.

name: SQL Injection in product search query
explain: User input is directly used in SQL query construction.
fix: Use Django ORM or parameterized queries.

name: Command injection via subprocess with shell=True in products
explain: Executing system commands with shell=True exposes the application to command injection.
fix: Avoid shell=True and pass commands as argument lists.
